Definition: from G5532; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of:--(have) need.
BiblicalUsage: To be in need is to lack something and feel it, and Jesus says the Father knows what we need before we ask. The friend at midnight calls for bread because of his persistence, not his politeness, and Paul asks the Romans to assist Phoebe because she is in need. The word covers both the lack and the asking.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God wants us to bring our needs to Him plainly, because He already knows them and still invites the asking. Need is not a failure of faith; it is the reason for prayer. I hold that a church that meets needs is a church that has understood the gospel.
